title: QUIC RFC 9000 Weakly Protected Packet Failure Policy
purpose: Describe the bounded S5P2 runtime policy for packet-protection open failures and weakly protected Initial and Handshake payload validation before mutable processing.
design_summary: The runtime treats packet-protection open failure as a discard once the matching Initial or Handshake keys are available. After a weakly protected packet opens, Initial and Handshake payloads are pre-validated before TLS crypto buffering, transcript advancement, ACK handling, or frame-specific side effects. Permitted control frames and CRYPTO frames can proceed; forbidden frames produce a local PROTOCOL_VIOLATION close. Malformed payloads that cannot be classified before processing remain discardable.
data_and_state_considerations: Payload pre-validation is intentionally placed after packet protection opens and before TryProcessHandshakePacketPayload mutates TLS ingress buffers, transcript state, recovery state, or connection-close state. This makes rollback explicit by preventing mutable content processing for weakly protected invalid payloads instead of trying to repair partial side effects later.
edge_cases_and_constraints: Initial packet authentication-tag failure leaves TLS ingress buffers and terminal state unchanged.
Handshake packet authentication failure with current keys does not commit transport parameters or defer the packet for retry.
Forbidden frames after otherwise valid weakly protected payload prefixes close with PROTOCOL_VIOLATION before the prefix mutates runtime state.
risks: Future Initial or Handshake frame allowances must update the shared weakly protected payload pre-validation table and the Section 12.4 requirement homes together.
Deferred replacement Handshake buffering remains valid only for packets whose expected replacement keys are not available yet.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the S5P2 weak-protection failure tail only. It does not claim broader packet-protection cryptographic correctness, Retry integrity validation changes, Version Negotiation behavior changes, public API widening, or hosted interop readiness.
